Subject: Sudden throughput collapse after model switch (v4q) — live impact

Priya,

We're seeing a severe throughput collapse in our prod inference pool since 02:00 UTC when your team flipped the v4 -> v4q quantized profile. p95 latency has gone from ~120ms to >900ms for many endpoints, and error rate (5xx) climbed to ~7% during the spike. This is blocking daytime traffic for our payments risk feature.

Attached is a short CSV of the SLO metrics over the last 6 hours and a screenshot from our dashboards. We need an explanation and a rollback plan — our CTO is on the line.

Can you confirm whether Redwood pushed any routing or batching changes alongside the qprofile? Also, please share any known incompatibilities for v4q with short prompt lengths (our typical seq=128).

Samir

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden throughput collapse after model switch (v4q) — live impact

Quick update from runtime triage: initial signs point to an unexpected decode-loop amplification when small sequences (<=160 tokens) hit the v4q execution path with our current kernel selection. That manifests as CPU spin on the host-side decoder threads and increased grpc timeouts to the worker, which in turn triggers request retries and pushes the observed 5xx.

What we've done so far:
- Scoped affected pool: us-east region, pool id=us-e-07 (Oxbridge dedicated)
- Temporarily disabled KV prefetch/cache for that pool to cut down on worker-side contention (partial improvement)
- Rolled model routing to fall back to v4 (non-quant) for a small canary subset — that restored p95 to ~170ms for canary traffic

Immediate ask:
- Need authorization to roll back Oxbridge's pool to v4 for all traffic now (safe, reversible).
- If we keep v4q, we will need to push a targeted qprofile tweak (reduce decoder micro-batching, change kernel) and run a short prod canary, estimate 4–6 hours to validate.

I'll attach the diagnostics tarball in the follow-up (stack traces, flame graphs, worker metrics).

Vivek

Following up on the actions and postmortem asks. Thank you team for the quick triage. Summary and next steps for execs: 

1) What happened: v4q profile introduced a decode micro-batching path that caused worker-side decode contention for short sequences on Oxbridge's traffic pattern. That surfaced as high p95 and elevated 5xx.
2) Immediate remediation: We rolled Oxbridge's dedicated pool us-e-07 back to v4 on 2027-06-05 at 11:35 UTC; p95 returned to ~140–180ms and 5xx dropped to <0.5% after traffic normalization.
3) Engineering fix: Vivek's team will ship qprofile revision (reduce decoder micro-batch, adjust kernel selection) and run a controlled canary next week (2027-06-09 window).
4) Customer remediation: Approved 30% service credit for impacted hours; Marissa to finalize customer-facing exec brief and credit paperwork.
5) Preventive ops: Add a preflight test for short-sequence workload patterns for qprofile flips and require dedicated canary schedule for reserved pools. Ops ticket created: OPS-1189.

I will prepare an exec brief for the CRO and CTO (including timeline and compensation). Priya/Marissa — please attach the diagnostics tarball in OPS-1189 and link the DocuSign amendment for credits.

Aditya
